page: Amazon Web Services c8i.xlarge is a compute-optimized virtual instance powered by the AWS Nitro System and an Intel Xeon 6975P-C processor running at 3.9 GHz. Built on the x86_64 architecture, the instance provides 4 dedicated virtual CPUs distributed across 2 physical cores with 2 threads per core. Memory capacity is 8.0 GB of high-frequency 7 GHz DDR5, establishing a 1:2 compute-to-memory ratio of 2.0 GB per vCPU. Hardware capabilities include Intel Advanced Matrix Extensions (AMX) and AVX-512 vector acceleration. The instance does not include bundled local storage or integrated GPUs, and it provides a 2 Gbps baseline network bandwidth.

Benchmark data reflects strong single-threaded CPU capability alongside modest multi-core throughput typical of a 2-core configuration. Single-core performance ranks in the upper quartile across tests, achieving 2177.0 in Geekbench single-core, 34.43 GB/sec in single-threaded gzip compression, and 14.31 GB/sec in single-threaded bzip3 decompression. In contrast, multi-threaded metrics such as stress-ng multi-core (4321.26) and multi-threaded bzip3 decompression (28.49 GB/sec) fall into the lower quartile, constrained by physical core limits. Geekbench multi-core (4953.0), Clang compilation (6065.0), and PassMark CPU (8047.87) sit in the middle 50% tier.

Memory bandwidth tests show 40.19 GB/sec for uncached read-only large blocks and 31.2 GB/sec for large block writes, both achieving mid-tier performance. For specialized tasks, the system supports small model inference, delivering 641.97 prompt processing tokens per second and 170.52 text generation tokens per second on a 135M parameter LLM. Operational throughput tests measure 8.21 million Redis SET operations per second and 8.23 GB/sec static web serving throughput.

Given its balance of high single-thread clock rates, modern vector instructions, and lean memory footprint, c8i.xlarge delivers cost-efficient compute capacity for workloads that demand processing speed over aggregate parallelism. The absence of local disk requires external network-attached storage integration. Best-fit workloads include CI/CD build nodes, microservices, batch processing tasks, web serving layers, and lightweight machine learning inference pipelines.
description: Amazon Web Services c8i.xlarge is a compute-optimized instance built on the Nitro hypervisor and powered by a 3.9 GHz Intel Xeon 6975P-C processor. The instance features an x86_64 architecture with 4 dedicated vCPUs mapped across 2 physical cores, paired with 8.0 GB of 7 GHz DDR5 memory at a 1:2 vCPU-to-RAM ratio. It includes support for Intel AMX and AVX-512 instruction sets, features no local storage or GPUs, and operates on a 2 Gbps baseline network link. Benchmark testing reveals top-quartile single-core metrics, including 2177.0 in Geekbench single-core and 34.43 GB/sec in gzip compression, while multi-core throughput remains modest due to the 2-core footprint. Delivering solid uncached memory throughput and 8.21 million Redis SET operations per second, the c8i.xlarge provides balanced resource density for compute-bound tasks, CI/CD compilation, web proxy serving, and small-model inference.
